newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares slide on downturn in Norsk Hydro.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares slide on downturn in Norsk Hydro.

text.p: Norwegian shares took a step backwards on Monday, dragged lower by industrial giant Norsk Hydro, which came under selling pressure following company comments on the outlook for second half profits.

Hydro said it expected earnings in the second half to be adversely affected by the recent drop in aluminium prices. It added that production problems at the Lille-Frigg gas condensate field in the North Sea meant that it may not fully recover its oustanding investment of 470 million crowns.
The comments were contained in a statement announcing a new issue of 20-year debentures in the U.S. market.
Hydro took a 755 million write-down on the Lille-Frigg project in the second quarter 1995 due to a revision in recoverable reserves.
The share retreated almost three percent, or 8.50 crowns to close at 304.50 crownsin 130 million crowns of trade.
Hydro has a weighting of abut 20 percent on Oslo's Total share index, which finished 0.63 percent off at 839.86 points.
Turnover was a bumper 1.53 billion crowns due to the buyout of passenger ferry company Larvik Line by Color Line, which accounted for 696 million crowns of business.
